{"self_assessment": "**Impact:** I picked up the pad early, backed Priya's fish idea, and sketched the layout: a nose start, a split into top and bottom body lines, and a fork at the tail. I also split the strokes among the four of us, so everyone was building within the first minute. Before the push, the run looked connected from the nose through both tail forks, about 100 of the 111 standing dominoes by our count. I can't say how the fish actually fell, since I'm writing right after the push.

**Execution:** I laid the full top line from the nose to the tail joint by about 2:45. The top line initially wasn't connected at the nose, and it took Priya several minutes to bridge that gap. I should have checked that joint as I started the line instead of finding out later. I did not fix the nose myself. Priya did, and I stayed clear of her. Later I lifted a couple of stray pale dominoes near the belly crossing, careful not to touch the dark line. After that I kept my hands off, which seemed right once the picture was connected.

**Collaboration:** I kept the table updated and handed out the strokes clearly. I gave way when Priya and Leo asked me to stay off the nose and the tail joint, so we avoided bumping each other. I held the pad longer than Priya may have wanted, though she told me to keep it. I also overstated that we were all set while a few pale strays were still around. Leo corrected a mix-up over who fixed the tail joint, and I didn't add to it.

**Leadership:** I set the plan and the stroke assignments early and kept morale up. The sketch was my main contribution. Priya led the nose repair and Tom led the final checks, and I think that was the right call. I kept my updates short and honest. Next time I would verify the first joint at the nose sooner instead of waiting for the line to show up pale."}
